subject.title: [Feature]: Mac app node reuses CLI node-host as one superset node

question: After the narrow Mac execution-policy repair, should OpenClaw sponsor an app-owned exact-version TypeScript worker as the canonical architecture for full CLI, MCP, plugin, and hosted-skill parity?
rationale: Current source proves the duplication and viable execution seam, but choosing the permanent transport, identity, packaging, lifecycle, and authorization owner is a product and security decision rather than a bounded bug repair.

options.title: Sponsor staged worker
options.body: Approve a staged design that first extracts the TypeScript command runtime and then integrates it behind the sole app-owned Gateway node with explicit security and upgrade gates.

options.title: Continue native parity
options.body: Keep Swift as an independent command-policy runtime and port each CLI capability separately, accepting ongoing cross-language duplication.

options.title: Move transport to CLI
options.body: Pursue a larger redesign where the CLI runtime owns the sole Gateway connection and migrate the app's device identity and pairing state.

recommendation.title: Sponsor staged worker
recommendation.body: Approve a staged design that first extracts the TypeScript command runtime and then integrates it behind the sole app-owned Gateway node with explicit security and upgrade gates.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue is assigned to steipete, and live history shows primary ownership of both sides of the proposed boundary.
